newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour says case for windfall tax strengthens.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour says case for windfall tax strengthens.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party said in a statement on Monday that the privatised water companies cut investment during last year's drought, which strengthens the case for a windfall tax.
The Labour Party said tax breaks given to water companies on privatisation had not produced promised increases in investment, but had instead paid for excess profits and boardroom abuse.
"The privatised utilities have lost any right to tax priveleges," said Alan Milburn, Labour's treasury spokesman in a statement.
"Labour's windfall levy on the excess profits of the privatised utilities will be used to help the many not the few," he added."
Labour said figures from British water industry regulator OFWAT show that half of the ten utility firms cut their overall investment on water supply and sewerage services in 1995/6.
It said Thames Water Plc had made the biggest cuts last year in water suppply investment, followed by North West Water Plc and Severn Trent Plc.
The statement said total investment by water companies has fallen by 27 percent in the last three years, and is now 335 million stg less than five years ago.

Milburn said the ruling Conservative government should legislate to stop the pay excesses throughout the privatised utilities, as well as setting compulsory targets for water companies to cut down on leakage.
